contents.reason: Rudin 6.12(c) is stated for his refinement (Darboux-Stieltjes) integral. This page defines the integral as a MESH limit (def-riemann-stieltjes-sum-and-integral), a strictly stronger notion, and under it unrestricted interval additivity is FALSE: when f and the integrator share a jump at the cut point c, the two pieces can be integrable while no mesh limit exists on [a,b] (cex-common-jump-prevents-riemann-stieltjes-integrability). thm-riemann-stieltjes-linearity-and-additivity therefore proves additivity under the correct hypothesis for this definition, namely f continuous at c, and Rudin’s unrestricted clause is not a missing result but a theorem about a different integral.

6.17 Theorem: reduction to an ordinary integral when the nondecreasing integrator has a Riemann-integrable derivative
contents.reason: Rudin 6.17 is proved for his refinement integral, where the Darboux comparison is available directly. Transporting it to this page’s mesh definition needs the refinement-versus-mesh equivalence as a separate development; thm-riemann-stieltjes-darboux-criterion supplies that equivalence only for a nondecreasing integrator together with a continuity-at-the-integrator-jumps side condition, which the merely-Riemann-integrable-derivative hypothesis does not give. The continuously differentiable case, where the side condition is automatic, is proved as thm-riemann-stieltjes-c1-integrator-reduction. The obstruction is the definitional divergence from the source, not an unbuilt lemma.
